content_voiceover: This table lines up the two classic pediatric bone sarcomas side by side, and it is a favorite way boards test you. Age helps separate them, Ewing sarcoma skews toward adolescents more than young children and is rare after age forty, while osteosarcoma peaks in adolescents and young adults and is rare under age five. Race is a clue too, Ewing sarcoma is notably rare in African and East Asian populations, while osteosarcoma shows no racial predilection. Predisposing factors are a big differentiator, Ewing sarcoma has no association with prior radiation and no known familial predisposition, whereas osteosarcoma is linked to radiation exposure and to cancer predisposition syndromes, specifically Li-Fraumeni syndrome from T P fifty-three mutations, and retinoblastoma. Ewing sarcoma classically causes constitutional symptoms like fever, while osteosarcoma usually does not. On imaging, Ewing sarcoma favors flat and long bones with a diaphyseal, shaft location and a laminated, onion-skin periosteal reaction, while osteosarcoma favors long bones, especially around the knee, in an epiphyseal or metaphyseal location, with a spiculated, sunburst pattern. Labs also diverge, Ewing sarcoma has a normal alkaline phosphatase but can show cytopenias if there's marrow involvement, while osteosarcoma classically raises alkaline phosphatase with a normal complete blood count. And histologically, Ewing sarcoma is a small round blue cell tumor driven by the E W S dash F L I one fusion, from a translocation between chromosome eleven band q twenty-four and chromosome twenty-two band q twelve, while osteosarcoma shows malignant spindle cells producing osteoid.
keypoints: Ewing sarcoma: diaphyseal, flat and long bones, onion-skin periosteal reaction, EWS-FLI1 fusion
Osteosarcoma: metaphyseal or epiphyseal, knee-predominant, sunburst periosteal reaction, elevated ALP
Osteosarcoma linked to Li-Fraumeni syndrome and retinoblastoma; Ewing has no known familial predisposition
Ewing sarcoma more often causes constitutional symptoms than osteosarcoma
Ewing sarcoma is rare in African and East Asian populations
keypoint_voiceover: Remember Ewing sarcoma as the diaphyseal, onion-skin, E W S dash F L I one tumor with constitutional symptoms and no familial link, versus osteosarcoma as the metaphyseal, sunburst, elevated alkaline phosphatase tumor tied to Li-Fraumeni and retinoblastoma predisposition.
